prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in League City, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1101; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for claim file purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable with us recording this statement?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection in League City?

A: I was driving through the intersection on a green light, heading east. I had the light and was going maybe thirty-five miles an hour. Then a car came from the left side and ran the red light. It hit the driver's side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the collision?

A: Only a second before. I tried to brake, but there wasn't enough time to avoid it.

Q: Were there any witnesses that you're aware of?

A: I think a man in a truck stopped at the corner. He got out and asked if I was okay. I didn't get his information, though.

Q: Let's talk about your injuries. Where were you hurt?

A: My right shoulder took most of the impact against the door frame. It's really sore, and I can't lift my arm above my head without pain.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care that same afternoon. They took X-rays and told me to follow up with an orthopedic specialist. I have an appointment scheduled for next week.

Q: Did you have any pain or injuries to other parts of your body?

A: My neck is a little stiff, but the shoulder is the main problem.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident?

A: Just that I was following the rules and I'm not sure why the other driver didn't stop. I'd like my car repaired and my medical bills taken care of.

Q: Thank you. We'll be in touch once we've reviewed the information. Have a good day.

A: Thanks, you too.
